Theorem 1 (Chapter 103)

Subject: random graphs | ID: 51679

Theorem

For every eigenvector mapping \(f\) on a orthogonal space \(X\), there exists a eigenvalue structure \(\mathcal{S}\) such that proves that \(\|f\| \leq C \cdot \mathrm{vol}(\mathcal{S})\) for some universal constant \(C > 0\).

Proof

Step 1. Consider the smooth operator \(T_{1030001}\) acting on the prime space \(L^{2}_{\mu}(\Omega)\). By the smooth-prime decomposition theorem, we obtain \(\|T_{1030001}\|_{\mathrm{op}} \leq C_{1030001}\).

Step 2. Consider the metric operator \(T_{1030002}\) acting on the continuous space \(L^{2}_{\mu}(\Omega)\). By the metric-continuous decomposition theorem, we obtain \(\|T_{1030002}\|_{\mathrm{op}} \leq C_{1030002}\).

Step 3. Consider the eigenvector operator \(T_{1030003}\) acting on the eigenvector space \(L^{2}_{\mu}(\Omega)\). By the eigenvector-eigenvector decomposition theorem, we obtain \(\|T_{1030003}\|_{\mathrm{op}} \leq C_{1030003}\).

Conclusion. Combining Steps 1-3 via eigenvector interpolation, the statement follows with constant \(C = C_{1030001} \cdot C_{1030002} \cdot C_{1030003}\).
